intervals.label: detector upgrade (third fill)
intervals.locator: snolab.ca, DEAP-3600 experiment page, status field
intervals.note: SNOLAB's experiment page (read 2026-09-17; an Internet Archive capture of 25 May 2026 shows the same status) gives the current status 'Upgrading'; no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives the true start date of this phase. The start is set to 2026-09, the month this status was first read, as the earliest defensible anchor rather than an invented date; see experiment:deap-3600 for the same reasoning. The collaboration's abstracts of 22 June and 21 September 2026 describe a "just-started" / "newly initiated third fill run" with preliminary third-fill results, which conflicts with reading SNOLAB's "Upgrading" label as a current absence of data taking; this interval is therefore a phase annotation and not the detector's current state. The SNOLAB page no longer loads (HTTP 404 on 2026-10-25). A 2025 plan said third-fill data taking would end "~ summer 2026" with decommissioning to make room for ARGOlite; no source consulted says whether that happened.

intervals.label: third fill: science operations
intervals.locator: Light Dark World 2026 talk (30 July 2026), summary slide; outline slide: 'Now taking data with detector in the upgraded configuration'; slide 'WIMP search': 'New data taking with upgraded detector to mitigate backgrounds (2025 – present)'
intervals.note: Start month not found: the 2025 plan had "Data taking 2025-November" and the CAP 2025 abstract expected the fill to complete in August 2025; the 2026 abstracts call it "just-started" / "newly initiated". Whether third-fill data taking is still running on 2026-10-25 is not stated (the 2025 plan ended it "~ summer 2026"; SNOLAB lists "Upgrading"). The newest dated statement is a 30 July 2026 talk by a DEAP collaboration member: "Now taking data with detector in the upgraded configuration", "New data taking with upgraded detector to mitigate backgrounds (2025 – present)", "New data collection in progress with upgraded DEAP-3600 at SNOLAB". That shows third-fill running at the end of July 2026 and gives the start year (2025) but not the month; the 21 September 2026 abstract ("newly initiated third fill run", preliminary results) is consistent. No source dated after 21 September reports the end of the run, so the 2025 plan's "~ summer 2026" end is not confirmed. Confidence is 'approximate': a talk is a rank-12 source and the start year is approximate.
intervals.quote: New data collection in progress with upgraded DEAP-3600 at SNOLAB

name: DEAP-3600 detector
notes: DEAP-3600 is a single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector, not a two-phase TPC: it has no drift field and no ionization/charge readout, and detects only scintillation light via its 255 PMTs (see the sourced 'technology' field above). Its technology classes list 'noble_liquid_tpc'/'argon_tpc' only because the available classes have no dedicated scintillator-only class; this is a classification accommodation, not a claim that DEAP-3600 has TPC charge readout.

Energy threshold: not recorded as a spec. The detector paper's design table (Table 1) gives a nominal analysis threshold of 15 keVee (electron-equivalent) for a 3 tonne-year exposure, not a nuclear-recoil energy; no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) states a single nuclear-recoil analysis energy threshold for DEAP-3600.

placements.quote: has been stably maintained since completing the second fill in November 2016

active_mass.note: This matches the 'approximately 3.3 tonne' figure quoted in the 2026 status paper (arXiv:2603.27372); consistent, not a conflict, with the 3600 kg design total_mass.
active_mass.quote: A final fill level corresponding to approximately 3300 kg LAr was chosen and has been stably maintained since completing the second fill in November 2016.

fiducial_mass.note: Design specification from Table 1 of the detector paper (design parameters for a 3-tonne-year exposure), not a measured fiducial mass of a particular analysis. The table's row label and value are separated in the extracted text.
fiducial_mass.quote: DEAP-3600 detector design parameters for a 3-tonne-year exposure. ... Fiducial mass, radius ... 1000 kg, 55 cm

phase.quote: The Dark matter Experiment using Argon Pulse-shape discrimination (DEAP) has been designed for a direct detection search for particle dark matter using a single-phase liquid argon target.

pmt_count.quote: The target volume is viewed by 255 8-inch-diameter ... Hamamatsu R5912-HQE high quantum efficiency (HQE) PMTs

shielding.locator: Astropart. Phys. 108 (2019) 1-23 (arXiv:1712.01982), Sec. 1 and Sec. 1.1 (Detector Overview)
shielding.note: The rock-overburden clause is also stated on deap3600.ca ('a deep underground laboratory which uses the 2 km of rock overburden to filter out cosmic-ray muons'); the water shield tank and muon veto are described in the detector paper.
shielding.quote: 2 km underground (6000 meters water equivalent overburden) at SNOLAB in Sudbury, Ontario ... The outer steel shell is immersed in a 7.8-m-diameter shield tank filled with ultra-pure water and instrumented with 48 Hamamatsu R1408 PMTs serving as a muon veto.
shielding.value: 2 km of rock overburden (6000 m.w.e.) at SNOLAB; the detector sits inside a 7.8 m diameter shield tank of ultra-pure water instrumented with 48 PMTs that serve as a muon veto.

target_medium.quote: using 3600 kg of liquid argon (LAr) as a target

total_mass.note: Design capacity; gives the experiment its name.
total_mass.quote: The cryostat consists of a 5-cm-thick spherical acrylic vessel (AV), 85 cm in inner radius which can contain 3600 kg of LAr.

description.note: TPB wavelength-shifter description from deap3600.ca ('tetraphenyl butadiene wavelength shifter to shift the ultraviolet (UV) light generated by argon scintillation to the visible region').
description.quote: The cryostat consists of a 5-cm-thick spherical acrylic vessel (AV), 85 cm in inner radius which can contain 3600 kg of LAr.
description.value: A 5-cm-thick spherical acrylic vessel, 85 cm inner radius, holding up to 3600 kg of liquid argon (fiducial volume 1000 kg within 55 cm radius), viewed by 255 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912-HQE PMTs that detect the 128 nm argon scintillation light after it is wavelength-shifted to the visible band by a tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) coating.

summary.plain: A sphere of 3.6 tonnes of liquid argon watched by 255 light sensors, 2 km underground in Canada. It looks for the faint flash of light a dark matter particle would make if it bumped into an argon atom, using only that light (no electric charge signal) to tell signal from background.
summary.technical: Single-phase LAr scintillation detector: 85 cm radius, 5 cm thick acrylic vessel, TPB-coated for VUV-to-visible wavelength shifting, holding a 3600 kg design/~3300 kg maintained fill (1000 kg, 55 cm-radius fiducial volume), read out by 255 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912-HQE PMTs. No drift field or charge readout; particle identification relies entirely on pulse-shape discrimination of the scintillation pulse. Located 2 km underground (6000 m.w.e.) at SNOLAB.

technology.locator: Astropart. Phys. 108 (2019) 1-23, Introduction; corroborated by deap3600.ca's description of a 'Single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector'
technology.quote: Particle energy deposition in the single phase LAr produces scintillation photons. The LAr scintillation time structure provides discrimination between WIMP-induced nuclear recoil events and electromagnetic background events.
technology.value: Single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector; unlike a two-phase argon or xenon TPC, DEAP-3600 has no drift field and no ionization/charge readout. It detects only scintillation light, collected by 255 PMTs, and uses the pulse shape of that scintillation signal (pulse-shape discrimination) to separate nuclear-recoil candidates from electromagnetic backgrounds.
